scope: Dated requirement-fit decisions for all four US-equities domain research layers, reconciled against existing September 21 runtime and execution records. The candidate slates are representative comparisons; all 152 historical cards remain in the original catalogs. Source review, native execution and measured tradeoffs remain distinct. No fresh installations, provider/model calls or broker actions were performed for this synthesis. A bounded primary-source quality refresh on September 21 America/New_York (September 22 UTC) corrects runtime/memory capability exclusions without changing broker, data or runtime qualification.

layers.title: Market data and reference
layers.requirement: Acquire licensed, source-identifiable US-equity observations; preserve feed, timestamps, identity and corporate actions; produce exact reproducible analytical snapshots and reject data whose historical availability or eligibility is unknown.
layers.current_choice: Official alpaca-py for the bounded selected market-data path; EdgarTools for selected filing parsing/acquisition; DuckDB and Parquet for local analysis; exchange_calendars for explicit session semantics. Dataset manifests and schema checks are requirements, while DVC/Pandera remain source-reviewed implementation candidates.
layers.rationale: Derived from domain row data-research (2026-09-22): Native acquisition, parsing and analytical receipts support these concrete interfaces without a new lake, broker or distributed database. They do not close the actual research bottleneck: a complete point-in-time eligible universe with trustworthy availability, identity and corporate-action semantics. Source-review defaults for DVC/Pandera must not be mistaken for installed acceptance. Databento/Massive are credible conditional alternatives when required coverage or rights cannot be obtained through the selected path.
limitations: The authenticated Alpaca receipt covers 25 AAPL SIP/raw daily bars and two corporate actions over five successful pages, not a survivorship-free universe, complete history or real-time feed entitlement.

Numeric corporate-action values matched the frozen probe, but missing dividend currency prevented full cash-unit reconciliation. Original historical availability and complete action coverage remain open.
Three documentary lifecycle cases preserve observed cutoffs and source anchors; retrospective claims do not establish historical as-known eligibility or permanent security identity.
The prior SEC HTTP 403 remains a historical failure. Later corrected acquisition and parsing qualify their selected requests only; no general filing-completeness or strategy-validity claim follows.
SQL, schemas and content hashes cannot repair missing provenance, revised fundamentals, access rights or outcome-selected samples.
layers.overturn_when: Freeze required universe/history/latency, rights, correction and availability semantics; compare selected providers on representative securities including delistings, ticker reuse and corporate actions, then change the feed/store only when a candidate closes those gaps with auditable records and acceptable measured cost. Add a server or lake only after local throughput/concurrency measurements justify it.

candidates.name: alpaca-py
candidates.rationale: The official SDK matches the chosen broker and provides measured bounded data acquisition plus a separately qualified paper smoke path. Historical source-only card language is superseded only for the exact later receipts, not all endpoints or entitlements.

candidates.name: EdgarTools
candidates.rationale: Selected SEC acquisition and native offline parsing preserve filing/document anchors. Keep the richer parser where that structured output is useful; original availability and historical security eligibility remain separate.

candidates.name: DuckDB
candidates.rationale: Native conversion, exact decimal/temporal checks and Parquet rereads fit the current local analytical workload. No comparative evidence currently requires a server merely to query these bounded artifacts.

candidates.name: exchange_calendars
candidates.rationale: The existing native XNYS fixture provides explicit session semantics in the analysis path. It does not qualify every holiday, emergency closure, extended-hours feed or security halt.

candidates.name: Databento
candidates.rationale: A reviewed candidate for licensed exchange-level history/replay and point-in-time reference data when those requirements exceed the selected acquisition path. No paid dataset or matched acquisition comparison was run for this choice.

candidates.name: Massive Python client
candidates.rationale: Consolidated data, reference and news interfaces warrant comparison against the exact required history, correction and permitted-use contract. Catalog inclusion is not subscription entitlement or coverage evidence.

candidates.name: OpenBB
candidates.rationale: A normalized research interface can remove bespoke adapters when several providers are required. It does not create data rights or missing history and currently adds another layer to an accepted direct SDK path.

candidates.name: sec-edgar-downloader
candidates.rationale: A smaller raw-filings collector is reasonable if structured EdgarTools parsing is unnecessary. No current gap warrants operating two overlapping collectors for the same source set.

candidates.name: Polars
candidates.rationale: Expression-based transforms may be clearer or faster for a defined workload. No same-data correctness/performance comparison presently justifies replacing the native SQL/Parquet path.

candidates.name: QuestDB
candidates.rationale: Sustained tick ingestion and concurrent time-series queries could justify a server. Current bounded files do not demonstrate that requirement, and no deployment benchmark is recorded.

candidates.name: ClickHouse
candidates.rationale: Shared large scans and aggregations can justify its operational footprint once measured local limits appear. This is a scale option, not a defeated competitor.

candidates.name: DVC
candidates.rationale: The historical default is a source-reviewed candidate for dataset hashes and dependency manifests. The selected portable runtime has no claimed DVC-native dataset acceptance; simple retained manifests do not imply DVC installation.

candidates.name: Pandera
candidates.rationale: A reviewed compact schema-validation candidate, with real market schemas and fail-closed promotion still requiring implementation. Schema acceptance cannot establish provider completeness or prevent every form of leakage.

candidates.name: lakeFS
candidates.rationale: Atomic object-store branches and promotion gates may serve concurrent teams. The present local snapshots have not established a need for that additional service.

candidates.name: yfinance
candidates.rationale: Convenient exploratory access does not satisfy the authoritative automated-trading data contract's rights and historical-quality requirements. The disposition is a requirement boundary, not a measured assertion that every returned price is wrong.

candidates.name: pandas exact timestamp support
candidates.rationale: Existing supporting dependency accepted for strict exact nanosecond timestamp parsing. Retain its tested contract alongside DuckDB/Parquet; this is not a general dataframe-performance win over Polars or Arrow.

winners.why_selected:
Among the adopted candidates, these three have retained receipts showing native execution of the acquisition, snapshot-storage and SEC reference steps that the requirement asks for. Adopted c3 exchange_calendars and c8 pandas also have native receipts, but they cover a session-calendar step and a parse step only (see alternatives). In each case the requirement's rejection and fail-closed behaviour comes from repository code running on top of these packages, not from the packages themselves.

(1) c9 alpaca-py 0.44.0 acquired licensed, source-identifiable observations and corporate actions. blueprints/us-equities/authenticated-data/native-receipt.json records native_cli_e2e 'native-alpaca-historical-20260920': 25 AAPL SIP/raw daily bars (3 pages) and 2 corporate actions (2 pages), with 5 HTTP 200 pages, observed terminal pagination and hash-anchored private artifacts. The bars matched the frozen LEAN probe 25/25 (maximum_absolute_close_difference "0.00"). The actions show numeric_values_equal 2 and unknown_currency 1, with status reconciliation_incomplete and original_historical_availability not_established. The comparison ran through the repository's compare.py, which is hard-wired to Alpaca and AAPL. catalogs/us-equities/runtime-target.json selects alpaca-py 0.44.0 for ingestion.

(2) c14 DuckDB 1.5.5 supplied the BIGINT/Parquet storage and reads for exact analytical snapshots. blueprints/us-equities/nanosecond-replay/receipt.json covers a SYNTHETIC fixture run natively through pandas 3.0.6 and DuckDB. It shows exact nanosecond cutoff selection and an identical early replay. The precision, overflow, overwrite and hash-mismatch rejections (exit_code 2) are enforced by the custom replay.py and point-in-time/temporal_snapshot.py contract (PIT.require and manifest checks), not by DuckDB (replay.py lines 30-41 and 115-137; DuckDB is used at lines 84-112 and 140-150). blueprints/us-equities/data/receipt.json records the Parquet sha256 of 6 LEAN simulation events on XNYS 2013-10-07. That receipt does not name DuckDB; the DuckDB use is visible only in blueprints/us-equities/data/summarize_backtest.py (lines 2, 8 and 19). blueprints/us-equities/lifecycle-sample/native-receipt.json lists duckdb 1.5.5 in its runtime, preserving source anchors and exact observation cutoffs over 6 HTTP 200 public documents through custom adapters.

(3) c6 EdgarTools 5.58.0 is the only adopted candidate with native SEC reference acquisition. blueprints/us-equities/catalyst-provenance/access-resolution.json native_upstream (lines 31-56) records get_filings with exit_code 0, http_status 200, cohort_rows 371, unique_accessions 360 and selected_context_rows 5. It names the original source URL and the complete compressed source sha256. The lifecycle-sample receipt records EdgarTools 5.58.0 in the offline processing that supports the ordered META ticker-reuse documentary evidence. EdgarTools did not produce the header acquisition or the unknown-availability rejection. The 5 headers came from the stdlib-only catalyst.py adapter (lines 57-65; its imports at lines 3-13 contain no edgar import). The historical packet (eligible_count 0, 5 before_first_availability at 2020-03-03) and the observed packet (5 qualified) also came from catalyst.py. The receipt itself says the provenance bridge is custom repository code (line 15). That rejection is therefore repository behaviour running over SEC data.

alternatives.name: Massive Python client
alternatives.why_not_default: The evidence is source review only. The data-research.json data-massive entry has decision 'conditional' and a native_workflow marked 'Prospective and UNEXECUTED'. There is no acquisition, entitlement or comparison receipt, and the repository has no Massive collector. The catalog notes that aggregate adjustment covers splits but not dividends. The packet's second evidence_ref, catalogs/us-equities/simulation-data-review.json, contains no Massive entry.

alternatives.name: Databento
alternatives.why_not_default: The evidence is source review only. The data-databento entry has decision 'conditional' and an UNEXECUTED workflow that may be billable. It is potentially stronger for licensed exchange-level history, point-in-time reference data and ts_event/ts_recv. However, there is no acquisition receipt, cost measurement, coverage comparison or collector in the repository. The exchange-specific feed is not consolidated US coverage, and corporate-action redistribution is restricted. simulation-data-review.json contains no Databento entry.

alternatives.name: exchange_calendars
alternatives.why_not_default: It has native evidence but is a complementary session-boundary dependency, not an acquisition or snapshot component. blueprints/us-equities/data/receipt.json records one XNYS session (2013-10-07, 13:30-20:00 UTC) via summarize_backtest.py. The catalog limitation says this does not cover every holiday, future schedule, venue, extended-hours session or halt. Retain it as the calendar companion.

alternatives.name: QuestDB
alternatives.why_not_default: The evidence is source review only. No server was installed or started. The catalog adopts it conditionally, for sustained tick ingestion after embedded files fail measured needs, but no throughput or concurrency measurement exists. Dedup/upsert can overwrite corrections unless a raw immutable ledger is kept.

alternatives.name: pandas exact timestamp support
alternatives.why_not_default: pandas 3.0.6 ran natively only as the timestamp parser (replay.py utc_ns, lines 30-41) in front of DuckDB, on synthetic clocks and symbols. The receipt states market_data_adapter_accepted false. It adds no independent acquisition or snapshot capability.

alternatives.name: Polars
alternatives.why_not_default: The evidence is source review only. The catalog lists Polars as an alternative to the SQL path and warns against duplicating a full SQL pipeline. There is no native receipt, and Polars supplies no data, corporate actions or point-in-time contract.

alternatives.name: ClickHouse
alternatives.why_not_default: The evidence is source review only. The command is prospective, and there is no server, throughput or reliability evidence. Background merges and deduplication are not an immutable revision ledger. The pin v26.8.7.19-lts is behind upstream v26.9.2.8-stable (packet pin_behind_upstream true).

alternatives.name: lakeFS
alternatives.why_not_default: The evidence is source review only. The catalog decision is 'alternative', aimed at concurrent teams that need atomic lake branches, and the quickstart is unexecuted. Commits do not make external databases part of an atomic snapshot, and garbage collection can remove historical artifacts.

alternatives.name: OpenBB
alternatives.why_not_default: The evidence is source review only; the workflow imports the router but makes no data request. Provider-normalized output does not normalize adjustment, time-of-availability or survivorship semantics. OpenBB is AGPL-3.0, and each provider's terms are separate.

alternatives.name: yfinance
alternatives.why_not_default: Not adopted. The catalog decision is 'excluded' because the data is for personal use and consists of present-day adjusted history and current tickers, so it cannot support point-in-time research.

alternatives.name: sec-edgar-downloader
alternatives.why_not_default: Not adopted. The catalog decision is 'alternative', a raw-only collector, and simulation-data-review.json records 'defer_redundant_downloader'. EdgarTools has a native get_filings receipt for the same SEC scope.

alternatives.name: Pandera
alternatives.why_not_default: Not adopted in this layer; it is the default in the data-quality layer. It is a schema-contract complement whose workflow is unexecuted and uses synthetic keys. Schema validation does not establish completeness, corporate actions or absence of leakage.

alternatives.name: DVC
alternatives.why_not_default: Not adopted in this layer; it is the default for data versioning. Its workflow is unexecuted. Content hashes prove identity, not validity or point-in-time correctness, and the winners' receipts already pin their artifacts by sha256.

layers.verdict_overturn_when:
Acquisition (c9): the repository currently has no runnable challenger arm. blueprints/us-equities/authenticated-data/compare.py reproduces only the c9 baseline. It loads alpaca-historical/collect.py (lines 15-20), verifies an Alpaca receipt (line 111) and rejects any symbol other than AAPL or any reference that is not exactly 25 sessions (lines 39-40 and 47-48). collect.py validate_plan also requires AAPL/sip/raw, alpaca_py_version 0.44.0 and data.alpaca.markets URLs (lines 125-143). The verdict should change only after an executed comparison meets all of the following:
- It uses a new provider-specific collector for Massive (c1) or Databento (c2). No such file exists yet.
- It uses a comparator generalized beyond Alpaca/AAPL.
- It runs against the same frozen blueprints/us-equities/authenticated-data/plan.json AAPL 2020-08-03..2020-09-04 contract plus representative delisted, ticker-reused (META) and dividend or split names.
- It shows the challenger reaching full corporate-action reconciliation (currency included) and auditable original historical availability where alpaca-py leaves them not_established, at acceptable measured request cost.
Until then, python3 blueprints/us-equities/authenticated-data/compare.py --run <run> --receipt-sha256 <sha> --lean <lean results> --lean-sha256 <sha> is the baseline check. The verdict should also be reopened if that baseline no longer reproduces 25/25 equal bars.

Snapshot store (c14): overturn if python3 blueprints/us-equities/nanosecond-replay/replay.py run on blueprints/us-equities/nanosecond-replay/fixture.json fails to reproduce the recorded selections and rejections. Also overturn if a measured throughput or concurrency test justifies a server (QuestDB c7 or ClickHouse c13).

SEC reference (c6): overturn if a native get_filings rerun through blueprints/us-equities/catalyst-provenance/native_edgar.py fails to reproduce the 371 rows and 360 unique accessions for the same day.

layers.verdict_overturn_when:
An executed comparison on one frozen plan of representative securities would change the verdict. The plan must include delistings, ticker reuse (FB/META/METV) and corporate actions, and the comparison must show another candidate closing the open gaps with auditable records. The gaps are original historical availability, dividend currency, complete action coverage and a permanent identity crosswalk.

The existing scripts cannot run the challenger arms as they are:
- blueprints/us-equities/alpaca-historical/collect.py hard-requires alpaca_py_version 0.44.0 (line 137), data.alpaca.markets URLs (line 142) and the alpaca SDK (lines 320-326).
- blueprints/us-equities/authenticated-data/compare.py accepts only an AAPL reference with exactly 25 sessions (lines 47-48).
- blueprints/us-equities/nanosecond-replay/replay.py implements only DuckDB materialize and select (lines 172-176).

So a Databento or Massive arm first needs a new provider collector and a generalized multi-symbol comparator, each with its own plan, hashes and verify step. A lakeFS, QuestDB or ClickHouse arm needs new store-specific replay code. That code must reproduce the select results on blueprints/us-equities/nanosecond-replay/fixture.json with identical cutoff selections and all four rejections, and the arm also needs a measured throughput or concurrency need. Identity continuity is re-checked with blueprints/us-equities/lifecycle-sample/sample.py verify-ledger in every arm.

layers.title: Storage and compute
layers.requirement: Acquire licensed, source-identifiable US-equity observations; preserve feed, timestamps, identity and corporate actions; produce exact reproducible analytical snapshots and reject data whose historical availability or eligibility is unknown.
layers.current_choice: Official alpaca-py for the bounded selected market-data path; EdgarTools for selected filing parsing/acquisition; DuckDB and Parquet for local analysis; exchange_calendars for explicit session semantics. Dataset manifests and schema checks are requirements, while DVC/Pandera remain source-reviewed implementation candidates.
layers.rationale: Derived from domain row data-research (2026-09-22): Native acquisition, parsing and analytical receipts support these concrete interfaces without a new lake, broker or distributed database. They do not close the actual research bottleneck: a complete point-in-time eligible universe with trustworthy availability, identity and corporate-action semantics. Source-review defaults for DVC/Pandera must not be mistaken for installed acceptance. Databento/Massive are credible conditional alternatives when required coverage or rights cannot be obtained through the selected path.
limitations: The authenticated Alpaca receipt covers 25 AAPL SIP/raw daily bars and two corporate actions over five successful pages, not a survivorship-free universe, complete history or real-time feed entitlement.

Numeric corporate-action values matched the frozen probe, but missing dividend currency prevented full cash-unit reconciliation. Original historical availability and complete action coverage remain open.
Three documentary lifecycle cases preserve observed cutoffs and source anchors; retrospective claims do not establish historical as-known eligibility or permanent security identity.
The prior SEC HTTP 403 remains a historical failure. Later corrected acquisition and parsing qualify their selected requests only; no general filing-completeness or strategy-validity claim follows.
SQL, schemas and content hashes cannot repair missing provenance, revised fundamentals, access rights or outcome-selected samples.
The us-equities catalog also tags entries for this taxonomy layer under foundation-memory (1), agents-operations (1); data-research (11) was picked as the primary group by entry count.
layers.overturn_when: Freeze required universe/history/latency, rights, correction and availability semantics; compare selected providers on representative securities including delistings, ticker reuse and corporate actions, then change the feed/store only when a candidate closes those gaps with auditable records and acceptable measured cost. Add a server or lake only after local throughput/concurrency measurements justify it.

layers.title: Data quality and orchestration
layers.requirement: Run bounded research with native identity and complete returned results; supervise owned processes; retain scoped telemetry, failed attempts and recoverable state without granting research workers broker execution authority.
layers.current_choice: Native Codex and Claude for bounded research and review; Dagu/systemd for selected local command workflows; one OpenTelemetry Collector with Prometheus/Loki/Grafana; native sandboxing and Restic for their separately qualified scopes. Optional gateways and agent frameworks remain task-specific.
layers.rationale: Derived from domain row agents-operations (2026-09-22): The retained native lane has actual task results, process/usage observations and local command workflow history. Adding an agent framework or gateway by default would not close a demonstrated requirement and can alter account identity, tool behavior or retry ownership. Dagu's accepted local scope fits existing commands; larger workflow and data platforms become preferable only when their durability, partitioning or operational requirements are real.
limitations: Native worker success and telemetry matching are bounded by the recorded task, process and account. They do not establish every native client/session, whole-task savings or unlimited allowance.
Dagu's older completed-history restart is not in-flight recovery. Later recovery receipts must be evaluated for their own process, host and workload rather than promoting all workflows.
Gateway transport health, routed text and ACP research acceptance do not establish native hook/tool parity or independent provider/model attestation.
Same-host recovery and configured restrictions do not establish off-host disaster recovery, a VM boundary, unattended broker operation or paid hosting.
The us-equities catalog also tags entries for this taxonomy layer under data-research (2); agents-operations (7) was picked as the primary group by entry count.
layers.overturn_when: Escalate to another scheduler, graph or host only when a specified long-running workflow, host-loss recovery, asset/backfill lineage or scale requirement exceeds the retained lane and the candidate passes the same failure, cancellation, output, identity and usage checks without duplicate effect owners.

candidates.name: Codex
candidates.rationale: The native CLI/app-server worker preserves the supported account, tool and session path and has real bounded research results. The official API Agents SDK is a different application integration, not an interchangeable subscription-backed worker.

candidates.name: Claude Code
candidates.rationale: Native independent review and research tasks have returned results and scoped usage observations. Retain this lane while checking actual account readiness and preserving failed or protocol-incomplete attempts.

candidates.name: Dagu
candidates.rationale: The native local scheduler runs existing bounded commands, retains authenticated history and has accepted research packet/Parquet preparation. The historical card's conditional label does not negate those later selected local operations.

candidates.name: OpenTelemetry Collector contrib
candidates.rationale: One accepted distribution supplies privacy transforms and native metric/log delivery. The core Collector repository is a source dependency, not a second collector to install.

candidates.name: Prometheus
candidates.rationale: The accepted metric store supports independently scoped process observations and alert rules. Historical missing initial samples remain limitations rather than retroactively repaired counts.

candidates.name: Loki
candidates.rationale: The existing privacy-filtered log lane complements metrics and has native process correlation evidence. It does not imply retention of full conversation transcripts.

candidates.name: Grafana
candidates.rationale: It reads the existing Prometheus/Loki stores and has retained dashboard evidence. A new trace/evaluation suite is conditional on a question the current observation stack cannot answer.

candidates.name: Restic
candidates.rationale: Native encrypted backup/restore plus original-application restoration now covers scoped ai-memory and Qdrant state. This supports current local recovery while leaving independent keys and off-host durability open.

candidates.name: Temporal
candidates.rationale: Durable activities, waiting and host-loss recovery are a plausible escalation for multi-day effects. The existing bounded command workload has not demonstrated the need or qualified a Temporal deployment.

candidates.name: Prefect
candidates.rationale: A Python-first flow service can fit scheduling/retries if that becomes the main operational requirement. It remains an alternative to adding another retry owner around current native workflows.

candidates.name: Dagster
candidates.rationale: Partitioned assets, lineage and backfills may justify adoption for the data program. Those merits do not establish benefit for simply dispatching a few native research workers.

candidates.name: LangGraph
candidates.rationale: Explicit agent state/checkpoints can help once branching and resume exceed a bounded native task. No matched task establishes that another agent loop is currently needed.

candidates.name: DeerFlow
candidates.rationale: One retained embedded DeerFlow ACP research prompt completed; current source also documents embedded Python, terminal, sandbox and Claude/native-provider integrations. These are substantial prebuilt capabilities, but the full planner/UI service and current revision have not been locally qualified. The tested adapter's read-only label mapped to workspaceWrite/on-request, so preserve that historical restriction finding rather than assuming the outer harness fixes it.

candidates.name: OmniRoute
candidates.rationale: Scoped installation, service and plaintext restore worked, while the September 20 inference attempt hit quota/429 limits and compression previews lost a required value. Keep optional explicit routing with compression disabled; these observations do not prove the gateway universally unusable.

candidates.name: FreeLLMAPI
candidates.rationale: The retained Windows-to-WSL health result proves transport only; Claude-like aliases can select local Qwen and do not establish Anthropic identity or Astra inference. It cannot silently replace the native worker.

candidates.name: OpenAI Agents SDK
candidates.rationale: Appropriate for an application-owned API agent with programmatic control when that is the requirement. It has not demonstrated a missing capability in the selected native Codex research path.

candidates.name: vLLM
candidates.rationale: Retain the accepted 0.25.0 WSL embedding runtime: 0.29.0 installed and its CLI ran, but GPU startup failed with unavailable UVA on this host. This is a concrete version/hardware boundary, not a failure of all newer releases or other hosts.

candidates.name: Deep Agents
candidates.rationale: The reviewed harness combines planning, delegated context, filesystem backends and LangGraph persistence. It is a credible prebuilt application-owned worker alternative, including local model routes; neither its README nor the available upstream tests establish better catalog-review accuracy, native-account compatibility or total cost on our tasks.

candidates.name: OpenHands SDK
candidates.rationale: The maintained SDK/Agent Server owns agents, tools, conversations, events and local or ephemeral workspaces; it is a credible isolated/remote-worker implementation. No matched native research, interruption/recovery or complete operating-cost comparison has displaced the accepted worker path.

candidates.name: OpenHands Agent Canvas
candidates.rationale: The current repository is Agent Canvas, a control center able to host OpenHands, Claude Code, Codex and other ACP agents across backends. Treat it as a prospective host for existing native workers, not merely a competing coding model. Its hosting, account boundaries, persistence and migration remain unqualified here.

candidates.name: Microsoft Agent Framework
candidates.rationale: The primary source provides .NET/Python agent applications, provider integrations and graph workflows with checkpoints and handoffs. It closes a source-review coverage gap, not a demonstrated runtime gap; qualify a required application workflow and deployment before adoption.

alternatives.name: Codex
alternatives.why_not_default: Codex is equally native-proven for completion and identity. blueprints/us-equities/workers/receipt.json records run.status completed, configured_model gpt-6-astra and total usage 135311 (lines 24-47). It also retains a failed ctx_execute_file attempt (lines 75-79 and 111), which is direct evidence of failed-attempt retention. In adoption/paired/receipt.json (lines 64-99) Astra completed with report validation passed. It is ranked below c9 for three reasons. (1) Broker authority is limited by the environment, not by configuration: workers/receipt.json line 110 says read-only mode does not restrict external MCP mutations and only that 'the recorded environment supplied no broker keys or broker tools'. The paired receipt (line 29) says Astra accepted only message items, but it records no exposed-tool count. (2) The retained evidence has no research-scoped telemetry match for Codex. foundation-native-20260920.json line 35 records only that native Codex usage matched Loki and Prometheus in the foundation run. (3) blueprints/us-equities/research-runtime/receipt.json lines 90-101 recorded codex_readiness.ready false (weekly usage 100%), and lines 148-152 record an unresolved device sign-in. The later paired receipt (line 207) records readiness restored. These are quota and sign-in failures, not capability failures. Codex remains the required first worker in the paired Astra-to-Claude graph and was left out only because of the 3-winner cap. The catalog's 'default' decision label (catalogs/us-equities/agents-operations.json lines 7-16) was not used as ranking evidence.

alternatives.name: OpenTelemetry Collector contrib
alternatives.why_not_default: The Collector is a required pipeline, not a competing choice. catalogs/us-equities/agents-operations.json (opentelemetry-collector-contrib entry, lines 854-894) says it supplies the privacy transform and OTLP delivery to Loki and Prometheus, and the Loki entry requires Collector sanitization before ingestion (line 1003). It forwards telemetry but does not retain it. It was left out of the winner set only because of the 3-winner cap and remains co-required.

alternatives.name: Prometheus
alternatives.why_not_default: Native usage matched Prometheus in the research-scoped query (blueprints/us-equities/research-runtime/receipt.json lines 112-113). Its series are aggregate counters (last_over_time of token_usage_tokens_total), not per-request records of failed attempts. In one run it missed the first two Claude requests during telemetry startup (evidence/receipts/foundation-native-20260920.json line 35). A fresh run that waited for initialization matched (line 36), so this is a startup-timing gap, not a proven retention defect. Prometheus complements Loki rather than replacing it.

alternatives.name: Restic
alternatives.why_not_default: Correction from the earlier proposal: Restic is the only candidate with executed restore receipts, so it partly covers the requirement's 'recoverable state' clause and is no longer marked out_of_scope. blueprints/us-equities/state-recovery/memory/receipt.json (kind native_cli_e2e, status passed_same_host_restore, lines 4-8) preserved 324 archived files and verified SQLite/FTS state. The Qdrant state-recovery receipt reports a same-host native restore of five collections and 201 points. The catalog's us_equities_fit (catalogs/us-equities/agents-operations.json line 1740) is 'Preserve selected reproducible research/configuration artifacts'. The catalog's limitation at line 1767 ('No live SQLite/Qdrant/Loki/Prometheus database ... was backed up') describes only the earlier public-file backup, and the later state-recovery receipts supersede it for SQLite and Qdrant. Restic is not the default here for three reasons: all restores were same-host; no Dagu run state, Loki or Prometheus store, or order journal was restored; and it does not run or supervise research. It was left out because of the 3-winner cap and because it covers worker memory and vector state, not run state.

alternatives.name: Grafana
alternatives.why_not_default: Grafana is a visualization layer. Correction from the earlier proposal: docs/dashboard-rendered-acceptance.md line 29 records that exact panel queries matched native memory, Qdrant and QMD results, not research-run telemetry. The same line says 'Claude has no current telemetry series; absence is not zero usage or savings.' Grafana does not run research, supervise processes or retain state itself.

alternatives.why_not_default: blueprints/us-equities/deerflow/research-receipt.json records one embedded invoke_acp_agent task that completed. The same receipt says DeerFlow discards ACP completion and usage, which had to be recovered from private adapter logs. It also says ACP read-only mode maps to workspaceWrite/on-request. No planner, UI, scheduler or hosted service was accepted. This falls short of the requirement for complete returned results and strict read-only scope.

layers.title: Evaluation and experiments
layers.requirement: Run bounded research with native identity and complete returned results; supervise owned processes; retain scoped telemetry, failed attempts and recoverable state without granting research workers broker execution authority.
layers.current_choice: Native Codex and Claude for bounded research and review; Dagu/systemd for selected local command workflows; one OpenTelemetry Collector with Prometheus/Loki/Grafana; native sandboxing and Restic for their separately qualified scopes. Optional gateways and agent frameworks remain task-specific.
layers.rationale: Derived from domain row agents-operations (2026-09-22): The retained native lane has actual task results, process/usage observations and local command workflow history. Adding an agent framework or gateway by default would not close a demonstrated requirement and can alter account identity, tool behavior or retry ownership. Dagu's accepted local scope fits existing commands; larger workflow and data platforms become preferable only when their durability, partitioning or operational requirements are real.
limitations: Native worker success and telemetry matching are bounded by the recorded task, process and account. They do not establish every native client/session, whole-task savings or unlimited allowance.
Dagu's older completed-history restart is not in-flight recovery. Later recovery receipts must be evaluated for their own process, host and workload rather than promoting all workflows.
Gateway transport health, routed text and ACP research acceptance do not establish native hook/tool parity or independent provider/model attestation.
Same-host recovery and configured restrictions do not establish off-host disaster recovery, a VM boundary, unattended broker operation or paid hosting.
The us-equities catalog also tags entries for this taxonomy layer under data-research (3), foundation-memory (3); agents-operations (6) was picked as the primary group by entry count.
layers.overturn_when: Escalate to another scheduler, graph or host only when a specified long-running workflow, host-loss recovery, asset/backfill lineage or scale requirement exceeds the retained lane and the candidate passes the same failure, cancellation, output, identity and usage checks without duplicate effect owners.

candidates.rationale: Scoped installation, service and plaintext restore worked, while the September 20 inference attempt hit quota/429 limits and compression previews lost a required value. candidates.name: FreeLLMAPI
candidates.rationale: The retained Windows-to-WSL health result proves transport only; Claude-like aliases can select local Qwen and do not establish Anthropic identity or Astra inference. It cannot silently replace the native worker.

candidates.name: OpenAI Agents SDK
candidates.rationale: Appropriate for an application-owned API agent with programmatic control when that is the requirement. It has not demonstrated a missing capability in the selected native Codex research path.

candidates.name: vLLM
candidates.rationale: Retain the accepted 0.25.0 WSL embedding runtime: 0.29.0 installed and its CLI ran, but GPU startup failed with unavailable UVA on this host. This is a concrete version/hardware boundary, not a failure of all newer releases or other hosts.

candidates.name: Deep Agents
candidates.rationale: The reviewed harness combines planning, delegated context, filesystem backends and LangGraph persistence. It is a credible prebuilt application-owned worker alternative, including local model routes; neither its README nor the available upstream tests establish better catalog-review accuracy, native-account compatibility or total cost on our tasks.

candidates.name: OpenHands SDK
candidates.rationale: The maintained SDK/Agent Server owns agents, tools, conversations, events and local or ephemeral workspaces; it is a credible isolated/remote-worker implementation. No matched native research, interruption/recovery or complete operating-cost comparison has displaced the accepted worker path.

candidates.name: OpenHands Agent Canvas
candidates.rationale: The current repository is Agent Canvas, a control center able to host OpenHands, Claude Code, Codex and other ACP agents across backends. Treat it as a prospective host for existing native workers, not merely a competing coding model. Its hosting, account boundaries, persistence and migration remain unqualified here.

candidates.name: Microsoft Agent Framework
candidates.rationale: The primary source provides .NET/Python agent applications, provider integrations and graph workflows with checkpoints and handoffs. It closes a source-review coverage gap, not a demonstrated runtime gap; qualify a required application workflow and deployment before adoption.

layers.title: Agents, models and workers
layers.requirement: Keep durable project knowledge, exact code and dated financial sources retrievable across native clients, with source recovery, explicit project scope and measurable retrieval quality.
layers.current_choice: ai-memory as the shared memory of record; QMD BM25 for documents; Serena for exact symbols; SocratiCode with Qdrant for conceptual code search; Context Mode and RTK for selected large outputs. These are complementary lanes, not one benchmark winner.
layers.rationale: Derived from domain row foundation-memory (2026-09-22): The selected lanes have native operation and recovery evidence on the existing host and avoid making every lookup depend on another extraction model or service. The measured QMD domain fixture returned the intended source in the first three results for 8 of 12 queries, so its low setup cost supports retention while the four misses require a representative comparison before claiming retrieval superiority. Memory recall and code search receipts do not qualify financial answer truth or historical market availability.
limitations: Twelve curated queries are a bounded diagnostic, not an independent holdout or a complete financial RAG evaluation. Exact-source recall at three was 8/12; misses remain recorded.

The eight native answer invocations form four within-provider task comparisons; two Claude full-context answers missed the word protocol and one focused Codex answer scored 9.5 versus 10. These are not general or causal savings results.
Same-host encrypted restore preserved application state, but independent key recovery, off-host durability and new-host client rebinding remain unqualified.
Alternative memory and RAG repositories below were generally source-reviewed, not run head-to-head. A source-only candidate has not failed.

Current primary-source review corrects manual-only, Claude-only and cloud-only exclusions. No matched memory benchmark or new installation was run; automatic capture, local providers and published scores remain source claims until exercised on the selected profile.
The us-equities catalog also tags entries for this taxonomy layer under agents-operations (10); foundation-memory (28) was picked as the primary group by entry count.
layers.overturn_when: Run a preregistered, representative held-out financial/document and code retrieval set at the same context budget; replace or supplement a lane only if a candidate improves source/answer fidelity, abstention and measured task cost while preserving isolation, exact source recovery and native client behavior.

candidates.name: ai-memory
candidates.rationale: Retain one shared project-scoped memory system because native capture/retrieval, maintenance and restoration have direct historical evidence. The fresh upstream source pin is review-only and does not replace the installed pin. This is the best-supported current operational fit, not a demonstrated recall, learning or cost winner.

candidates.name: QMD
candidates.rationale: The local BM25 lane requires no model weights and has native search/get/update evidence. Its 8/12 exact-source recall at three bounds the claim; retention remains conditional on a representative comparison.

candidates.name: Serena
candidates.rationale: Language-server symbol/reference retrieval fits exact source editing; native Python/TypeScript coverage was repaired and exercised. This complements document and semantic search instead of replacing them.

candidates.name: SocratiCode
candidates.rationale: Native indexing, watcher and conceptual retrieval already use the scoped local embedding service. Keep that operational path while acknowledging hardware, licensing and reindexing requirements.

candidates.name: Qdrant
candidates.rationale: The vector store is already integrated with the selected semantic lane. A native snapshot/restore preserved five collections, 201 points and one exact query; that is operational evidence, not comparative retrieval quality.

candidates.name: Context Mode
candidates.rationale: Useful native calls retain large output outside the prompt and retrieve focused sections. Counters are connection-level estimates; native use and retained recovery do not establish avoided provider billing.

candidates.name: RTK
candidates.rationale: Supported CLI filtering has clean-userspace and hosted Linux fixture evidence, including raw proxy fidelity and error retention. It is selected for matching outputs, not an automatic filter for every source.

candidates.name: Mem0
candidates.rationale: The current project provides application user/session/agent memory and temporal retrieval with published reproducible evaluation references. It is a serious application-memory candidate; a same-task project-continuity and cost comparison remains absent, and benchmark claims do not transfer automatically.

candidates.name: Hindsight
candidates.rationale: Priority comparison for retain/recall/reflect and temporal or experiential memory. Current upstream explicitly documents local providers and native Codex/Claude subscription providers, so missing API credentials alone is not a valid exclusion. Published benchmarks are not a matched test of our project recall, source fidelity, boundaries or operating cost.

candidates.name: OpenViking
candidates.rationale: Hierarchical context filesystem unifies resources, memory and skills with scoped retrieval and inspectable session-derived Markdown. Consider it if fragmented context becomes a measured obstacle; published benchmarks and the AGPL deployment model need workload-specific evaluation before replacing current scoped lanes.

candidates.name: Graphiti

layers.title: Observability and hosting
layers.requirement: Run bounded research with native identity and complete returned results; supervise owned processes; retain scoped telemetry, failed attempts and recoverable state without granting research workers broker execution authority.
layers.current_choice: Native Codex and Claude for bounded research and review; Dagu/systemd for selected local command workflows; one OpenTelemetry Collector with Prometheus/Loki/Grafana; native sandboxing and Restic for their separately qualified scopes. Optional gateways and agent frameworks remain task-specific.
layers.rationale: Derived from domain row agents-operations (2026-09-22): The retained native lane has actual task results, process/usage observations and local command workflow history. Adding an agent framework or gateway by default would not close a demonstrated requirement and can alter account identity, tool behavior or retry ownership. Dagu's accepted local scope fits existing commands; larger workflow and data platforms become preferable only when their durability, partitioning or operational requirements are real.
limitations: Native worker success and telemetry matching are bounded by the recorded task, process and account. They do not establish every native client/session, whole-task savings or unlimited allowance.
Dagu's older completed-history restart is not in-flight recovery. Later recovery receipts must be evaluated for their own process, host and workload rather than promoting all workflows.
Gateway transport health, routed text and ACP research acceptance do not establish native hook/tool parity or independent provider/model attestation.
Same-host recovery and configured restrictions do not establish off-host disaster recovery, a VM boundary, unattended broker operation or paid hosting.
layers.overturn_when: Escalate to another scheduler, graph or host only when a specified long-running workflow, host-loss recovery, asset/backfill lineage or scale requirement exceeds the retained lane and the candidate passes the same failure, cancellation, output, identity and usage checks without duplicate effect owners.

layers.title: Security and supply chain
layers.requirement: Run bounded research with native identity and complete returned results; supervise owned processes; retain scoped telemetry, failed attempts and recoverable state without granting research workers broker execution authority.
layers.current_choice: Native Codex and Claude for bounded research and review; Dagu/systemd for selected local command workflows; one OpenTelemetry Collector with Prometheus/Loki/Grafana; native sandboxing and Restic for their separately qualified scopes. Optional gateways and agent frameworks remain task-specific.
layers.rationale: Derived from domain row agents-operations (2026-09-22): The retained native lane has actual task results, process/usage observations and local command workflow history. Adding an agent framework or gateway by default would not close a demonstrated requirement and can alter account identity, tool behavior or retry ownership. Dagu's accepted local scope fits existing commands; larger workflow and data platforms become preferable only when their durability, partitioning or operational requirements are real.
limitations: Native worker success and telemetry matching are bounded by the recorded task, process and account. They do not establish every native client/session, whole-task savings or unlimited allowance.
Dagu's older completed-history restart is not in-flight recovery. Later recovery receipts must be evaluated for their own process, host and workload rather than promoting all workflows.
Gateway transport health, routed text and ACP research acceptance do not establish native hook/tool parity or independent provider/model attestation.
Same-host recovery and configured restrictions do not establish off-host disaster recovery, a VM boundary, unattended broker operation or paid hosting.
layers.overturn_when: Escalate to another scheduler, graph or host only when a specified long-running workflow, host-loss recovery, asset/backfill lineage or scale requirement exceeds the retained lane and the candidate passes the same failure, cancellation, output, identity and usage checks without duplicate effect owners.

domain_rows.title: Scoped memory and research retrieval
domain_rows.requirement: Keep durable project knowledge, exact code and dated financial sources retrievable across native clients, with source recovery, explicit project scope and measurable retrieval quality.
domain_rows.current_choice: ai-memory as the shared memory of record; QMD BM25 for documents; Serena for exact symbols; SocratiCode with Qdrant for conceptual code search; Context Mode and RTK for selected large outputs. These are complementary lanes, not one benchmark winner.
domain_rows.rationale: The selected lanes have native operation and recovery evidence on the existing host and avoid making every lookup depend on another extraction model or service. The measured QMD domain fixture returned the intended source in the first three results for 8 of 12 queries, so its low setup cost supports retention while the four misses require a representative comparison before claiming retrieval superiority. Memory recall and code search receipts do not qualify financial answer truth or historical market availability.
limitations: Twelve curated queries are a bounded diagnostic, not an independent holdout or a complete financial RAG evaluation. Exact-source recall at three was 8/12; misses remain recorded.

The eight native answer invocations form four within-provider task comparisons; two Claude full-context answers missed the word protocol and one focused Codex answer scored 9.5 versus 10. These are not general or causal savings results.
Same-host encrypted restore preserved application state, but independent key recovery, off-host durability and new-host client rebinding remain unqualified.
Alternative memory and RAG repositories below were generally source-reviewed, not run head-to-head. A source-only candidate has not failed.

Current primary-source review corrects manual-only, Claude-only and cloud-only exclusions. No matched memory benchmark or new installation was run; automatic capture, local providers and published scores remain source claims until exercised on the selected profile.
domain_rows.overturn_when: Run a preregistered, representative held-out financial/document and code retrieval set at the same context budget; replace or supplement a lane only if a candidate improves source/answer fidelity, abstention and measured task cost while preserving isolation, exact source recovery and native client behavior.

domain_rows.rationale: The retained native lane has actual task results, process/usage observations and local command workflow history. Adding an agent framework or gateway by default would not close a demonstrated requirement and can alter account identity, tool behavior or retry ownership. limitations: Native worker success and telemetry matching are bounded by the recorded task, process and account. They do not establish every native client/session, whole-task savings or unlimited allowance.
Dagu's older completed-history restart is not in-flight recovery. Later recovery receipts must be evaluated for their own process, host and workload rather than promoting all workflows.
Gateway transport health, routed text and ACP research acceptance do not establish native hook/tool parity or independent provider/model attestation.
Same-host recovery and configured restrictions do not establish off-host disaster recovery, a VM boundary, unattended broker operation or paid hosting.
domain_rows.overturn_when: Escalate to another scheduler, graph or host only when a specified long-running workflow, host-loss recovery, asset/backfill lineage or scale requirement exceeds the retained lane and the candidate passes the same failure, cancellation, output, identity and usage checks without duplicate effect owners.

domain_rows.title: Simulation, broker adapters and strategy qualification
domain_rows.requirement: Use the selected NautilusTrader destination with broker-specific execution boundaries, deterministic numeric risk and reproducible equity accounting; preserve the prior LEAN oracle and qualify any strategy with causal data, costs and independent reconciliation.
domain_rows.current_choice: NautilusTrader 2.0.0rc5 is the user-selected destination; LEAN remains the retained historical comparison engine. Nautilus native IBKR awaits broker acceptance; Alpaca uses official alpaca-py and a separately qualified deterministic paper path. No strategy is promoted as profitable.
domain_rows.rationale: The current choice follows the explicit runtime target and supported native IBKR direction, with real installation/replay and bounded AAPL accounting evidence. LEAN has deeper retained SPY stress/dividend/cash evidence and is kept as the comparison oracle rather than relabeled a losing engine. The AAPL diagnostic and one Alpaca paper roundtrip do not prove SPY parity, realistic liquidity, IBKR operation, continuous paper service or a winning strategy. Existing research modules remain task-specific.
limitations: Nautilus 2.0.0rc5 is a prerelease. The old September 19 Nautilus alternative and LEAN default cards remain historical; runtime-target.json governs the current destination.

The retained AAPL replay has 15 bars and five roundtrips per baseline/stress scenario with reconciled cash; it excludes known action dates and uses retrospective synthetic close fills with unlimited modeled depth.
SPY/LEAN dividend/cash parity is still planned. LEAN's known-crash fixtures are engineering stresses, not untouched holdout results or calibrated broker execution.

The Alpaca trial observed two actual writes, a -0.08 USD cash-matched gross result, flat/idle reconciliation and completed-trial recovery with zero additional writes. In-flight native failure cases, IBKR, live operation and continuous paper operation remain open.
No accepted point-in-time universe, extreme-mover/catalyst strategy, financing-inclusive performance or deployable profitability follows from these receipts.

Independent source review found two bare matches! expressions that do not assert denial-event variants in Nautilus risk tests, also present in v2.0.0rc5 source. Other tests assert denial and reasons. This narrow test defect is not an observed runtime failure; see docs/blind-catalog-source-adjudication-20260921.md.
domain_rows.overturn_when: Reopen the implementation choice if Nautilus cannot preserve a required cash/order semantic, fails a preregistered SPY/LEAN parity tolerance, or a broker-specific adapter cannot pass ownership, reconciliation, partial/cancel/reconnect and numeric risk cases. Compare alternatives on the same frozen inputs and failure contract; promote a strategy only after independent temporal and cost-aware evaluation.

candidates.name: NautilusTrader
candidates.rationale: The explicit current destination is 2.0.0rc5 with supported native IBKR integration. Native synthetic and bounded AAPL replays support continued qualification, not superiority over every engine or completed broker acceptance.

candidates.name: LEAN
candidates.rationale: Retain as the historical comparison engine: six frozen SPY simulations exercised fill/fee/dividend cash reconciliation and a buying-power rejection. It is no longer the current destination, and those stresses do not establish profitable strategy behavior.

candidates.name: alpaca-py
candidates.rationale: The official SDK has a separately implemented bounded deterministic paper lifecycle and one reconciled long-to-flat trial. It is not a native Nautilus Alpaca adapter and must retain one owned writer.

candidates.name: LEAN Alpaca brokerage
candidates.rationale: Native patched adapter compilation is retained evidence, but initialization/account entitlement and this adapter's paper execution remain unqualified. The separate alpaca-py smoke does not close its gate or restore the historical default route.

candidates.name: Lumibot
candidates.rationale: A direct Python strategy lifecycle with Alpaca support is a substantial alternative. It needs the same data, risk, order/recovery and accounting comparison before replacing the selected destination.

candidates.name: vectorbt
candidates.rationale: Array-based sweeps can accelerate a defined research task, subject to semantics and license fit. Selected signals would still require event-driven accounting and execution checks; no matched speed/quality result is recorded here.

candidates.name: Backtrader
candidates.rationale: Useful for an existing strategy or bounded offline comparison; its reviewed integration age weakens the case for a new second Alpaca host. No general engine failure was measured.

candidates.name: backtesting.py
candidates.rationale: Small OHLC prototypes fit signal sanity checks, but do not meet the selected portfolio order-state and reconciliation-host requirement by themselves.

candidates.name: Zipline Reloaded
candidates.rationale: Maintained continuation is relevant for existing Zipline/Pipeline research. It has no recorded same-input advantage that warrants a second active event engine in this stack.

candidates.name: ib_async
candidates.rationale: IBKR is now selected, so the old 'only if later selected' rationale is historical. This community client remains an alternative to the selected native Nautilus adapter, with no local broker/recovery comparison establishing a need to switch.

candidates.name: skfolio
candidates.rationale: Native 1.2.9 WalkForward evaluation produced 20 development folds and one reserved period with causality assertions. This qualifies a raw-price label control module, not portfolio PnL, optimization superiority or broker risk enforcement.

candidates.name: Qlib
candidates.rationale: A structured factor/model experiment framework can help after a defensible US point-in-time dataset exists. Its broader workflow does not cure the current provenance/eligibility gaps or justify another active strategy stack yet.

candidates.name: FinRL
candidates.rationale: RL remains an experiment after deterministic and supervised baselines; no local out-of-sample, cost-aware strategy or execution qualification supports promoting it.

candidates.name: TradingAgents
candidates.rationale: The reviewed multi-agent financial analysis workflow is a research candidate. More agents and a simulated decision pipeline do not establish causal data, alpha or authority to bypass deterministic order/risk code.

candidates.name: PyPortfolioOpt
candidates.rationale: A smaller classical allocation module can be preferable when allocation alone is required. The selected skfolio study qualifies chronological evaluation, not a head-to-head proof that its optimizers dominate this candidate.

candidates.name: Dockerized IB Gateway
candidates.rationale: The selected Nautilus source supports optional DockerizedIBGateway alongside an external native TWS/Gateway. Image digest, sign-in, restart, API connectivity and broker reconciliation are not qualified; this is independent of Alpaca acceptance.
